dashboard.empty: You don't have any evaluations yet.

evaluation.languagesHint: Fixed scale: 1 Spanish only, 3 two languages, 5 three languages.
evaluation.observationsHint: Optional. Give the AI context on what the numbers do not say.
evaluation.privacyNote: The AI receives the role, the scores and the notes. Not the name.
evaluation.narrativeMissingHint: This evaluation was saved without an automatic write-up. The score is valid all the same.
evaluation.needsPerson: Choose who you are evaluating first.
evaluation.needsScores: Some blocks still have unanswered questions.
evaluation.title: Evaluation
evaluation.subtitle: Blocks weighted by role. The server computes the average and the AI drafts the write-up.
evaluation.savedChanges: Changes saved. The previous write-up no longer matches these scores: generate it again.
evaluation.showDeletedHint: Deleted ones do not count on the dashboard, but they stay here so you can restore them.
evaluation.confirmDeleteBody: It will stop counting on their dashboard and in their history. It is not removed from the database: you can restore it by ticking “Show deleted” in the list.
evaluation.deletedNotice: Evaluation deleted. You can restore it from the list.
evaluation.deletedWarning: This evaluation is deleted: it does not count on the dashboard or in the history.

users.title: Users
users.name: Name
users.passwordHint: At least 12 characters. The person can change it after signing in; it is never emailed.
users.confirmDeactivateBody: All their open sessions will be closed and they will not be able to sign in until reactivated. The account is not deleted.
users.leadHint: Only people with the Lead or Administrator role can be a lead.
users.emailHint: This is what they sign in with. Changing it does not close their open sessions.
users.selfRoleHint: You cannot change your own administrator role.
users.newPasswordPlaceholder: Leave blank to keep the current one
users.newPasswordHint: At least 12 characters. Changing it closes all their open sessions and they will have to sign in again.
users.orphanedReports: {count} person(s) still reported to them: give them another lead.

catalogs.title: Catalogues
catalogs.deactivateHint: These are deactivated, not deleted: users and evaluations reference them.
catalogs.confirmDeactivateBody: It can no longer be assigned to anyone. It is not deleted: users and evaluations already using it keep it, and you can reactivate it right here.
catalogs.showInactiveHint: Deactivated entries stay in the list, marked as such.

apiKeys.title: External API
apiKeys.intro: Keys that let other systems —the Lexart platform above all— create users in Cube without signing in here. Each key only works from the IPs and domains you declare for it.
apiKeys.name: Name
apiKeys.nameHint: Who it is for. For example: Lexart platform (production).
apiKeys.scopesHint: With no permissions the key authenticates but cannot do anything.
apiKeys.allowlistHint: By default it is accepted from nowhere: holding the key is not enough. IPs cover server-to-server calls; domains cover calls from a browser (Origin header).
apiKeys.allowlistEmpty: No entries. The key is blocked.
apiKeys.blockedHint: It has no authorised IP or domain, so it will not work from anywhere.
apiKeys.tokenBody: This is the only time it is shown: Cube only stores its hash. If you lose it, create another one and deactivate this one.
apiKeys.confirmDeactivateBody: The system using it will stop being able to create users on its next call. The key is not deleted: you can reactivate it right here.
apiKeys.usageBody: The key travels in the X-API-Key header. The whoami endpoint does nothing but return the IP and origin Cube actually saw, which is what you need to authorise here.
